name: 2019 livery
description: White, with the rear fuselage teal behind a straight diagonal lime-green line that runs from the belly ahead of the tail up to the fin; a big light green shamrock on the teal fin; teal engines; 'Aer Lingus' in teal with a small green shamrock above the forward windows.

logos.description: The Aer Lingus shamrock, simplified in 2019: three heart-shaped leaves round a point with a short curved stem, flat light green, large on the teal fin. Measured 2026-11-27 on EI-LRH (A321neo) and EI-DES (A320), left sides fitted to their shapes: the same on both, its leaves x 0.28-0.70 and y 0.03-0.60 at its middle, centered at x 0.54, y 0.315. Not symmetric: the top leaf leans aft, the stem curves down toward the leading edge, the same picture on both sides (not mirrored).
The shamrock again, small, just after the 'Aer Lingus' title: aft of it on the left.
The same after the title as read from the right: forward of it, just behind door 1.
A small Irish tricolor just after the registration, under the rear windows.

titles.style: The 2019 Aer Lingus wordmark: a clean medium-weight geometric sans, capital A and L, above the forward windows behind door 1.

notes: Measured on A321neo EI-LRH (left side side-on, right side from below). The diagonal is a straight line in side view. The aircraft names under the forward windows and the reg on the fin tip are not drawn. A330s and A320s share the scheme; some A320ceos may still wear the 1990s scheme (white over green belly, 'aer lingus' in green, green fin with the white shamrock) until repainted. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on EI-LRH (left side, near side-on, 2025-04-30): the title runs x 0.143-0.262, its baseline about 0.25 m over the window tops and its capitals about 0.5 m tall (it had sat higher, y 0.47); lowercase 0.63 of the capitals; the straight diagonal reduced to its ends. 2026-11-27: the small shamrock after the title placed per side, as EI-DES shows it (A320, left 2026-07-23, right 2026-04-16): aft of the title on the left, forward of it on the right, just behind door 1 (one place for both had it sitting on the title's 'g'); on the A320 the left one further aft (types.A320). 2026-11-27: the fin's shamrock re-placed from the photos: bigger (its leaves 0.56 of the fin's height) and further aft (centered x 0.54, y 0.315), the same on the A320 (EI-DES) and the A321neo (EI-LRH); it had sat small and forward at x 0.36. Its mark (Skyarium's EIN/shamrock) is now traced off EI-LRH.
history: Replaced Skyarium v1's approximation (2026-11). The 2019 scheme replaced the green-belly livery with the white shamrock on a green tail.

A320.note: On the A320 the title runs further aft for its length (x 0.167 to 0.33 on EI-DES's left side, 2026-07-23), so the small shamrock after it on the left sits at x 0.35.
